_about: Verified news for each 2025 Hotlist project. Every item cites a source. Applied to src/page.html by scripts/apply_updates.py. Researched October 2026.

city-in-the-forest.status: Completed (99 min). On the festival circuit; sales by CAA, festival distribution by The Film Collaborative

updates.text: New York premiere at DOC NYC (November 11 to 19) in the Big Blue section.
Screened at DokuFest in Prizren, Kosovo, in the Human Rights Dox competition.
Won Best Documentary Feature at the Nashville Film Festival, a Special Mention at DokuFest, and a Jury Special Mention at DMZ Docs.
World premiere at Sheffield DocFest in the International First Feature Competition, where it received a Special Mention.

manhood.status: Completed (91 min). In theaters from October 28, 2026, digital from November 17. US streaming on World of Wonder; UK on the BBC

updates.text: Theatrical release opens in Los Angeles on October 28 and New York on October 30, followed by digital release on November 17. World of Wonder holds US streaming rights and the BBC has UK broadcast and iPlayer rights.
New York premiere at IFC Center as part of DOC NYC Selects: Summer 2026, with a conversation with director Daniel Lombroso.
World premiere at SXSW on March 14, with reviews in Variety, IndieWire and The Hollywood Reporter.

earth-to-michael.status: Completed (91 min). Premiered at Telluride 2025; on the festival circuit

updates.text: East Coast premiere at DC/DOX in Washington, DC.
Premiered at the Telluride Film Festival in the Backlot program.

thank-you-for-listening.status: Completed. Streaming on Yahoo; presented by Texas Monthly

laurels.event: Yahoo x Nonfiction Hotlist Film Festival

updates.text: Screened at the first Yahoo x Nonfiction Hotlist Film Festival at the American Dream center in East Rutherford, New Jersey, with Joshua Ray Walker performing.
Streaming exclusively on Yahoo from August 19, presented by Texas Monthly. Selected as one of 20 films from nearly 1,000 submissions for the Yahoo x Nonfiction Hotlist slate.

Debuted at the Dallas International Film Festival, screened at Raindance in London, won the Audience Award for short film and Best Texas Short Film at the Waco Independent Film Festival, and completed a limited theatrical run in Los Angeles.

making-the-line.status: World premiere at the Hawaiʻi International Film Festival, October 22, 2026. Raising $80,000 for final post-production

updates.text: World premiere at the Hawaiʻi International Film Festival on October 22 at Consolidated Theatres Kāhala. The team is raising $80,000 for final post-production.

when-we-all-get-to-heaven.status: Released as a ten-part series on Outward, Slate's LGBTQ podcast

updates.text: Released as a ten-episode series through Outward, Slate's LGBTQ podcast. The Gay & Lesbian Review called it beautifully written, edited, and produced.
Awarded a Rainin Filmmakers with Disabilities Grant from SFFILM, in post-production.
Selected for the Sundance Institute Documentary Edit Residency, following a 2024 Sundance Documentary Film Grant.
Named a 2026 Sundance Institute Sandbox Fund grantee in the production category.
Emma D. Miller was a Jewish Film Institute Filmmaker in Residence with Father Figures.
Selected for Catapult Film Fund's tenth Rough Cut Retreat cohort.
